messages.author: a5e83218c834e013
messages.subject: RStan Release Process
parts:
We need to formalize the RStan release process, or at least fix
how dependencies work on CRAN. I gave a tutorial today with
about 50 attendees that was fucked because most of them
(not surprisingly) waited until the last second to install RStan
from CRAN and all got bit by the RStan/StanHeaders clash.
Besides the embarrassment it took substantial amount of time
away from the tutorial. We have to be able to do better.

parts:

We need to formalize the RStan release process, or at least fix
how dependencies work on CRAN.  I gave a tutorial today with
about 50 attendees that was fucked because most of them
(not surprisingly) waited until the last second to install RStan
from CRAN and all got bit by the RStan/StanHeaders clash.
Besides the embarrassment it took substantial amount of time
away from the tutorial.  We have to be able to do better.

If I had known you were giving a tutorial today, I could have mitigated it somewhat with instructions on how to install it from Git or something. But there is not much we can do about CRAN. CRAN separately approved both StanHeaders and rstan within a few hours but getting binaries built and mirrored takes a few days and at any moment someone could get versions that are out of sync.

Ben

messages.author: a5e83218c834e013
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] RStan Release Process
parts:
I understand the limitations of CRAN, but we need to find
some way around it.  

For example, why were the dependencies updated so early?  
Shouldn’t StanHeaders have been submitted first, and then
only when it had been built and deployed RStan submitted?

If there’s no way to ensure a consistent way to propagate
changes to the dependencies then we at least need a status
alert somewhere, whether it be on Jenkins or the mailing
list or Twitter where (a) these kinds of submit windows can
be announced and (b) queried at any time to make it easy
to identify that it’s a CRAN issue.

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] RStan Release Process
parts: On Wednesday, January 6, 2016 at 3:41:12 AM UTC-5, Michael Betancourt wrote:

For example, why were the dependencies updated so early?  
Shouldn’t StanHeaders have been submitted first, and then
only when it had been built and deployed RStan submitted?
That is what happened. StanHeaders 2.9.0 started to mirror out when rstan was still on 2.8.2. Due to one of the refactors, rstan 2.8.2 couldn't compile models with StanHeaders 2.9.0.

If there’s no way to ensure a consistent way to propagate
changes to the dependencies then we at least need a status
alert somewhere, whether it be on Jenkins or the mailing
list or Twitter where (a) these kinds of submit windows can
be announced and (b) queried at any time to make it easy
to identify that it’s a CRAN issue.

We talked about that a little at the meeting. That is possible. I hadn't done that previously because I thought it would create more confusion to say something like "StanHeaders++ is available on CRAN but don't download it yet".

But definitely if someone is doing a workshop or something, we should avoid uploading during that time and have backup installation procedures ready.

Ben

messages.author: cab04b8f0759c712
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] RStan Release Process
parts:
On Wed, Jan 6, 2016 at 11:13 AM, Ben Goodrich <goodri...@gmail.com> wrote:
On Wednesday, January 6, 2016 at 3:41:12 AM UTC-5, Michael Betancourt wrote:
For example, why were the dependencies updated so early?  
Shouldn’t StanHeaders have been submitted first, and then
only when it had been built and deployed RStan submitted?

That is what happened. StanHeaders 2.9.0 started to mirror out when rstan was still on 2.8.2. Due to one of the refactors, rstan 2.8.2 couldn't compile models with StanHeaders 2.9.0.
 
If there’s no way to ensure a consistent way to propagate
changes to the dependencies then we at least need a status
alert somewhere, whether it be on Jenkins or the mailing
list or Twitter where (a) these kinds of submit windows can
be announced and (b) queried at any time to make it easy
to identify that it’s a CRAN issue.

We talked about that a little at the meeting. That is possible. I hadn't done that previously because I thought it would create more confusion to say something like "StanHeaders++ is available on CRAN but don't download it yet".

We should be proactive about known problems. I think we should:
- describe the problem clearly
- post a workaround on stan-users; sticky the post
- put the workaround on the rstan wiki in a prominent place: for example https://github.com/stan-dev/rstan -- update the README.md so it shows up there.
 
Once that's up, we can put it up on twitter too.
But definitely if someone is doing a workshop or something, we should avoid uploading during that time and have backup installation procedures ready.
I really don't think this should concern our release process. We have to consider that there are always new users, courses, classes, etc. and we should just post a workaround that works.

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] RStan Release Process
parts:
On Wednesday, January 6, 2016 at 11:34:57 AM UTC-5, Michael Betancourt wrote:
What I don’t get is why RStan 2.8.2 pointed to the updated StanHeaders
instead of the 2.8.0 version.  Do CRAN dependencies not target specific
versions?  Is that not something that we can force?

Not with that much control. You can specify that rstan 2.8.2 only works with StanHeaders 2.8.0, but if StanHeaders 2.9.0 is available it will just refuse to install rather than fetching StanHeaders 2.8.2. To actually get stuff done, you would have to manually install StanHeaders 2.8.0.

Ben

messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] RStan Release Process
parts:
On Wednesday, January 6, 2016 at 11:49:52 AM UTC-5, Michael Betancourt wrote:
I agree.  At least that way we’d know what was going on instead of getting
weird compiler errors.

Refusing to install would be slightly better than installing but not working. But it means that it is impossible for me to do a patch fix of StanHeaders without also updating rstan, which could be a problem with the embargo on uploads within a month. In other words, if some function in Math was returning the wrong result, I could have done a StanHeaders 2.8.0-1 while leaving rstan 2.8.2 as is. So, if we have to utilize workarounds to get it to actually work during the major transition periods, I would rather maintain the ability to update them asynchronously when they don't break.

Ben

I think it's a whole lot better. The principle is to fail as early as possible
in any computational process with decent warning messages.

> But it means that it is impossible for me to do a patch fix of StanHeaders without also updating rstan, which could be a problem with the embargo on uploads within a month. In other words, if some function in Math was returning the wrong result, I could have done a StanHeaders 2.8.0-1 while leaving rstan 2.8.2 as is. So, if we have to utilize workarounds to get it to actually work during the major transition periods, I would rather maintain the ability to update them asynchronously when they don't break.

I'd accept that tradeoff.

Having some kind of up-to-date outside-of-CRAN way to install is
also necessary to mitigate the situation of CRAN and mirrors
being out-of-synch.

- Bob

messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] RStan Release Process
parts:
On Wednesday, January 6, 2016 at 5:39:39 PM UTC-5, Michael Betancourt wrote:
I would prefer to have the package not even install, but at the very
least the warning has to be obvious.  Spending a third of a tutorial
running around tracking down include errors is not an okay
circumstance.

If rstan doesn't install, we have no control over the error message because the error will come from base::install.packages(). It will just say something like installation failed. If we allow rstan to install and throw an error when it tries to compile with a mismatched StanHeaders, then we can error with a customized message and a link to the wiki page.

Ben
